name: Velrath Guava-Black Pepper Tonic
description: A sophisticated tonic water elevated with real guava extract and a measured dose of black pepper oil, producing a soda that functions as a standalone drink or a mixer. Velrath has built its reputation on restraint — nothing is oversaturated.
flavor_profile: Crisp quinine bitterness, sweet guava mid-note, then a slow-building black pepper warmth that spreads across the chest — dry and elegant
cultural_context: Velrath is the soda of choice in Tier 3-4 bars that take their non-alcoholic offerings seriously. It's ordered by people who know exactly what they want and don't feel the need to explain it. Bartenders across GLMZ respect Velrath as a mixer — it doesn't compete with the spirit, it converses with it.
story_hooks: Velrath's black pepper supplier — a vertical farm co-op in the outer ring — has just had its land claim contested by a corponation subsidiary; if the co-op loses, Velrath loses its real-extract status
A Tier 4 private club has been serving Velrath tonic in bottles that look exactly like a restricted pharmaceutical compound — the resemblance may not be accidental
A food critic who gave Velrath a withering review two years ago has since become its most vocal advocate; she will not explain what changed her mind
